<description>
Fix a stale persistent coin lock when a temporary coin lock is upgraded to persistent.

Previously, upgrading an existing non-persistent lock to a persistent lock used `emplace()` without updating the existing value. As a result, the in-memory lock remained non-persistent.

When the coin was later spent, `UnlockCoin()` therefore did not erase the persistent `LOCKED_UTXO` database record. After restarting the wallet, the stale lock was loaded again.

This change updates the existing lock state when the coin is already present.

Adds a functional test covering:
- temporary coin lock
- upgrade to persistent lock
- spending the locked coin
- wallet reload
- verification that the spent lock is not restored

Fixes #36304
</description>

[2026-10-04] c:5975240001 comment by ArvinFarrelP (contributor):
Good catch. `insert_or_assign` could downgrade an existing persistent lock when `LockCoin()` was called non-persistently. I've changed the implementation to preserve the persistent state when the coin is already locked, and added a regression test for this case. `wallet_basic.py` passes with the new test.
[2026-10-04] c:5975483009 comment by jcastros:
Tested ACK 23dbc1fe5c.

The downgrade is gone. I locked a coin persistently, spent it with `fundrawtransaction` `lockUnspents=true`, and `listlockunspent` stayed empty across `unloadwallet` / `loadwallet` (`gettxout` null). Same with `sendall`, that coin in `inputs`, and `lock_unspents=true` (`"complete": true`).

`wallet_basic.py` passes. Putting `insert_or_assign` back in `LoadLockedCoin` fails the new check at [wallet_basic.py:239](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/23dbc1fe5cc02bb3afa681b530f8ebdecdd9a51a/test/functional/wallet_basic.py#L239) with `not(1 == 0)`.
